content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Multi-region failover alert: attempted shift from us-east-1 -> ap-southeast-1 failed to converge. us-east-1 still serving ~40% of traffic despite weights set to ap-southeast-1=85 at 02:10 UTC. Error spike + client timeouts observed. Paging on-call.
Maya Singh: I'm oncall, joining. quick summary please?
incident-bot: Shift initiated 02:05 UTC by routing-controller. Health probes for ap-southeast-1 reported transient 503s at 02:08; controller retried but route convergence stalled. Observed persistent TCP socket affinity to us-east-1 because of long keep-alives and DNS TTL=180.
Owen Park: Looking at edge logs now. CDN edge shows ~38% upstream selection to us-east-1 from APAC edges. Many clients maintain TLS session reuse; ALB stickiness present for a subset.
Devon Carter: App metrics: model-worker pool in ap-southeast-1 showing high GPU queue wait times, cold-start latency for large models. Pods restarted a few times during warm-up -> readiness flapping around 02:07-02:09.
Rhea Kapoor: Support: several streaming customers in APAC reporting stalls and reconnect loops. Dedicated tenant X reported embedding requests timing out. Marking customer impact: Sev2 (partial regional outage for APAC streaming).
Maya Singh: Mitigation plan proposals: 1) Pause auto-routing controller. 2) Force connection drain on us-east-1 NLBs. 3) Reduce DNS TTL to 30s. 4) Warm model pools in ap-southeast-1 and scale up. Who takes DNS and who does drain?
Owen Park: I'll handle connection drain and edge settings. Starting NLB target deregistration delay -> 5s and ALB idle timeout -> 10s. Note: this may drop long-lived streams briefly.
Devon Carter: I'll warm ap-southeast-1 model pool, pre-pull weights, and set temporary nodeCount +40%. Also increasing pod memory for heavy models. Commands I ran:
```
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/model-worker --replicas=12
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/model-worker PRELOAD_MODELS=true
```
ops-bot: Automation: routing-controller paused by Maya at 02:14 UTC.
Maya Singh: Owen, confirm drain applied. Rhea, prep a short customer message: "We observed partial failover convergence; engineers are draining legacy region and warming new region. Some long-lived streams may need reconnecting. ETA 30m." Please include dedicated support contact.
Owen Park: ALB/NLB deregistration change applied. Also toggled proxy to send FIN to idle connections. tcpdump on edge shows many sockets with TTL 300s; even after DNS change some clients still reuse old connections.
Rhea Kapoor: Posted status update to status.redwood: "Partial regional failover impacting APAC streams; mitigation in progress. Engineers draining old region and warming new region. Updates every 10 minutes." Escalated critical customers.
incident-bot: Route53 TTL update requested at 02:18 UTC to 30s for api.redwood.example. Change ID Z-678901.
Devon Carter: Warm pool coming up. Preloaded models for heavy endpoints. Readiness probes now steady at 02:22 UTC.
Owen Park: Early metrics: us-east-1 traffic share down to 18% after drain. However some customers behind ISP resolvers still hitting east due to cached DNS; reducing TTL helps future shifts.
Maya Singh: Good. Two risky items: client TCP stickiness and provider-level routing asymmetry for some prefixes. Owen, can you run traceroutes for affected prefixes and open provider ticket if needed?
Owen Park: Running traceroutes. For a subset of APAC edges, traceroute shows preferred path to us-east-1 due to older BGP advertisement on direct-connect. Opening ticket with provider (CLOUD-555321), attaching pcap and traceroute.
Devon Carter: Noted a herd of OOM kills in model-worker logs from earlier; I've increased JVM/XLA headroom and set pod anti-affinity to spread workers across hosts. Also adding a pre-shift check to fail fast if restart_count > 2 in last 10m.
Rhea Kapoor: Support update: Customer Y reported reconnecting fixed their stream. Customer Z on Dedicated still seeing occasional 504s; SE engaged.
incident-bot: Metric snapshot 02:30 UTC: us-east-1 traffic ~9%, 5xx trending down to baseline, but p99 latency in APAC still +120ms for some routes. Recommended maintain manual weights ap-southeast-1=95/us-east-1=5 for 20m.
Maya Singh: We'll hold at 95/5 for 20m, then move to 100/0 if stable. Also schedule post-incident items: pre-warm model cache, lower default maintenance TTLs, add BGP path verification pre-check. Assign owners.
Owen Park: Provider ticket CLOUD-555321 opened with pcap/traceroute. Provider responded: no fabric outage, but observed stale advertisement from partner peer. They've asked partner to refresh route advertisement.
Devon Carter: Post-incident actions: implement warmup job triggered before any weighted shift, and increase autoscaler cooldown to avoid aggressive pod churn during shifts.
Rhea Kapoor: Status page update at 02:38 UTC: "Mitigation effective; majority traffic now on ap-southeast-1. Some customers may need to reconnect. A follow-up postmortem will be published." :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Reminder: create incident doc and assign severity. Suggested Sev2. Create ticket P-3250009876.
Maya Singh: I'll create the incident doc and run 30m blameless postmortem in next 48h. Handoff: I'll remain till 02:50 UTC then hand to infrastructure lead. If any regression, escalate to on-call manager.
Owen Park: Keeping watch on provider ticket; will update if partner refreshes routes.
Devon Carter: All model workers stable and ready by 02:36 UTC. Rolling restart avoided.
Rhea Kapoor: Customer comms: sent short note to impacted customers and set SEs on standby. Noting templates for reconnection guidance to include in runbook.
incident-bot: Final snapshot 02:42 UTC: us-east-1 traffic 1.1%, 5xx baseline, latency improving. Recommend keep monitoring until 03:00 UTC then close if stable.
Maya Singh: Thanks everyone. After closure let's make the pre-shift checklist mandatory and add runbook steps for connection draining commands and customer messaging. :thumbsup:
